```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r settings}
START_YEAR = 2023
raw_dir  = "../data/raw"
proc_dir = "../data/processed"
library(dplyr)
```

Every cleaned table ends up keyed by `ticker` and, for the quarterly ones, `year` + `quarter`.
Those are the keys `03_merge` joins on.

## Read the raw data

```{r read}
nareit_list   = readr::read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "nareit_list_raw.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
nareit_detail = readr::read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "nareit_detail_raw.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
sec_facts     = readr::read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "sec_companyfacts_raw.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
pr_index      = readr::read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "press_release_index.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
llm_raw       = readr::read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "llm_press_release_extract.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
dgs10_raw     = readr::read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "fred_dgs10_raw.csv"), col_types = "cc")
prices_raw    = readr::read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "yahoo_prices_raw.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Clean each source

### Nareit directory (one row per REIT)

The list page packs three things into one string (`KIM | Jericho, New York | Retail`), and
the numbers come in as text with `%` and `$` signs. The profile page labels have extra
"View definition" link text glued on, so we strip that before reshaping long to wide.

```{r clean-nareit}
list_clean = nareit_list |>
  tidyr::separate_wider_delim(ticker_line, delim = "|",
                              names = c("ticker", "hq_location", "nareit_sector"),
                              too_few = "align_start", too_many = "merge") |>
  mutate(across(c(ticker, hq_location, nareit_sector, company), stringr::str_squish),
         hq_city  = stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_extract(hq_location, "^[^,]+")),
         hq_state = stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_extract(hq_location, "(?<=,).+$")),
         price_on_nareit = readr::parse_number(price_text),
         nareit_as_of    = as.Date(substr(as_of, 1, 10))) |>
  select(ticker, company, detail_path, hq_city, hq_state, nareit_sector, price_on_nareit, nareit_as_of) |>
  distinct(ticker, .keep_all = TRUE)    # a REIT should only appear once

detail_wide = nareit_detail |>
  mutate(label = label |> stringr::str_remove("View definition") |> stringr::str_squish(),
         value = stringr::str_squish(value)) |>
  filter(!is.na(label)) |>
  distinct(detail_path, label, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = label, values_from = value)

# if no REIT on the site has a field (e.g. the site drops one), add it as empty so the code still runs
expected_labels = c("Exchange", "Address", "1-Year Total Return", "3-Year Compound Annual Total Return",
                    "5-Year Compound Annual Total Return", "10-Year Compound Annual Total Return",
                    "Dividend Yield", "Trailing Year Dividends per Share")
for (lab in setdiff(expected_labels, names(detail_wide))) detail_wide[[lab]] = NA_character_

detail_clean = detail_wide |>
  transmute(
    detail_path,
    exchange          = stringr::str_extract(Exchange, "(?<=\\()[A-Z]+(?=\\))"),
    hq_zip            = stringr::str_extract(Address, "\\b\\d{5}\\b"),
    return_1yr_pct    = readr::parse_number(`1-Year Total Return`),
    return_3yr_cagr_pct  = readr::parse_number(`3-Year Compound Annual Total Return`),
    return_5yr_cagr_pct  = readr::parse_number(`5-Year Compound Annual Total Return`),
    return_10yr_cagr_pct = readr::parse_number(`10-Year Compound Annual Total Return`),
    dividend_yield_pct   = readr::parse_number(`Dividend Yield`),
    trailing_dividend_ps = readr::parse_number(`Trailing Year Dividends per Share`)
  )

nareit_clean = list_clean |>
  left_join(detail_clean, by = "detail_path") |>
  select(-detail_path)
glimpse(nareit_clean)
```

Notes: the multi-year returns are blank for REITs that have not been public that long
(Curbline only listed in late 2024). We leave those as `NA` rather than filling them in.

### SEC XBRL facts (one row per REIT per quarter)

Each SEC fact has a `start` and `end` date (balance sheet values only have `end`). We use
those dates to decide what period a number covers:

- no `start` date and `end` on a quarter-end = a balance sheet value at the end of that quarter (assets, liabilities)
- about 3 months between `start` and `end` (80-100 days) = a quarterly income statement value
- about 12 months (350-380 days) = a full-year value
- anything else (6 or 9 month year-to-date totals) is dropped

We first tried the SEC's `frame` label for this, but the SEC leaves it blank on some facts
(for example NNN's Q1 2025 revenue), which left holes in the data. The dates are always there.

Companies only file 10-Qs for Q1-Q3, so most fourth quarters do not exist as a three-month
number. We back out **Q4 = full year - Q1 - Q2 - Q3**, and only when all three quarters are present.

```{r clean-sec}
facts = sec_facts |>
  filter(unit == "USD") |>
  mutate(start = as.Date(start), end = as.Date(end),
         days  = as.numeric(end - start),
         period_type = case_when(
           is.na(start) & end == lubridate::ceiling_date(end, "quarter") - 1 ~ "instant",
           days >= 80  & days <= 100 ~ "quarter",
           days >= 350 & days <= 380 ~ "year",
           TRUE ~ "other")) |>
  filter(period_type != "other") |>
  arrange(desc(filed)) |>
  distinct(ticker, tag, start, end, .keep_all = TRUE) |>     # same number re-reported in later filings
  mutate(year    = as.integer(lubridate::year(end)),
         quarter = as.integer(lubridate::quarter(end)),
         instant = period_type == "instant")

# balance sheet: assets and liabilities at quarter end
balance = facts |>
  filter(instant, tag %in% c("Assets", "Liabilities")) |>
  distinct(ticker, tag, year, quarter, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(ticker, year, quarter, tag, val) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tag, values_from = val)
if (!"Liabilities" %in% names(balance)) balance$Liabilities = NA_real_
balance = balance |> rename(total_assets = Assets, total_liabilities = Liabilities)

# income statement: quarterly values plus a derived Q4
quarterly = facts |> filter(period_type == "quarter") |>
  distinct(ticker, tag, year, quarter, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(ticker, tag, year, quarter, val)
annual = facts |> filter(period_type == "year") |>
  distinct(ticker, tag, year, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(ticker, tag, year, annual_val = val)

q4_derived = quarterly |>
  filter(quarter %in% 1:3) |>
  group_by(ticker, tag, year) |>
  summarise(n_q = n(), q1_q3 = sum(val), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(annual, by = c("ticker", "tag", "year")) |>
  filter(n_q == 3) |>
  transmute(ticker, tag, year, quarter = 4L, val = annual_val - q1_q3)

flows_q = bind_rows(
  quarterly |> mutate(q4_derived = FALSE),
  q4_derived |> mutate(q4_derived = TRUE)
) |>
  arrange(q4_derived) |>
  distinct(ticker, tag, year, quarter, .keep_all = TRUE)   # if a real Q4 exists, keep it

# REITs use different tags for the same idea: pick the first one that exists
income = flows_q |>
  select(ticker, tag, year, quarter, val) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tag, values_from = val)
for (col in c("Revenues", "OperatingLeaseLeaseIncome", "NetIncomeLoss",
              "NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic", "ProfitLoss")) {
  if (!col %in% names(income)) income[[col]] = NA_real_
}
income = income |>
  transmute(ticker, year, quarter,
            revenue    = coalesce(Revenues, OperatingLeaseLeaseIncome),
            revenue_source = case_when(!is.na(Revenues) ~ "Revenues",
                                       !is.na(OperatingLeaseLeaseIncome) ~ "OperatingLeaseLeaseIncome"),
            net_income = coalesce(NetIncomeLoss, NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic, ProfitLoss))

q4_flag = flows_q |>
  filter(tag %in% c("Revenues", "OperatingLeaseLeaseIncome")) |>
  group_by(ticker, year, quarter) |>
  summarise(revenue_q4_derived = any(q4_derived), .groups = "drop")

sec_clean = full_join(income, balance, by = c("ticker", "year", "quarter")) |>
  left_join(q4_flag, by = c("ticker", "year", "quarter")) |>
  filter(year >= START_YEAR) |>
  mutate(revenue_mm      = revenue / 1e6,
         net_income_mm   = net_income / 1e6,
         total_assets_mm = total_assets / 1e6,
         liabilities_to_assets = total_liabilities / total_assets) |>
  select(ticker, year, quarter, revenue_mm, net_income_mm, total_assets_mm,
         liabilities_to_assets, revenue_source, revenue_q4_derived) |>
  arrange(ticker, year, quarter)
glimpse(sec_clean)
```

### LLM press release extract (one row per REIT per quarter)

The LLM tells us which quarter each release covers. We also work out the quarter from the
filing date (a release filed in Jan-Mar is about Q4 of the year before, Apr-Jun about Q1,
and so on). The two should agree; `04_validate` lists any that do not. When they disagree we
trust the filing date, because it comes straight from the SEC.

Some REITs file more than one Item 2.02 8-K in a quarter (a correction, or an extra update).
We keep the latest one per REIT per quarter.

```{r clean-llm}
llm_clean = llm_raw |>
  inner_join(pr_index |> select(file, ticker, accessionNumber, filingDate), by = "file") |>
  mutate(
    filingDate = as.Date(filingDate),
    filed_month = lubridate::month(filingDate),
    year    = as.integer(lubridate::year(filingDate)) - if_else(filed_month <= 3, 1L, 0L),
    quarter = case_when(filed_month <= 3 ~ 4L, filed_month <= 6 ~ 1L, filed_month <= 9 ~ 2L, TRUE ~ 3L),
    llm_period_matches = (period_year == year & period_quarter == quarter)
  ) |>
  filter(year >= START_YEAR) |>
  arrange(desc(filingDate)) |>
  distinct(ticker, year, quarter, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(ticker, year, quarter, filing_date = filingDate, accession = accessionNumber,
         property_focus, occupancy_pct, same_property_noi_growth_pct, ffo_per_share,
         core_ffo_per_share, rent_spread_pct, guidance_change, net_debt_to_ebitda,
         llm_period_year = period_year, llm_period_quarter = period_quarter, llm_period_matches, file)

# The model labels property type once per release; a REIT should get one label.
# Use the label it got most often.
focus_by_reit = llm_clean |>
  count(ticker, property_focus) |>
  group_by(ticker) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(ticker, property_type = property_focus)

# A simpler three-way grouping for the dashboard
focus_by_reit = focus_by_reit |>
  mutate(property_group = case_when(
    property_type %in% c("grocery_anchored_center", "open_air_center") ~ "Shopping centers",
    property_type == "mall_outlet" ~ "Malls & outlets",
    property_type == "net_lease"   ~ "Net lease",
    TRUE ~ "Mixed"))
focus_by_reit
```

### FRED 10-year Treasury (one row per quarter)

FRED uses `"."` for days with no value (holidays). Those become `NA` and are dropped.

```{r clean-fred}
dgs10_daily = dgs10_raw |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), dgs10 = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value))) |>
  filter(!is.na(dgs10))

dgs10_q = dgs10_daily |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(lubridate::year(date)), quarter = as.integer(lubridate::quarter(date))) |>
  group_by(year, quarter) |>
  summarise(treasury_10y_avg = mean(dgs10),
            treasury_10y_end = dgs10[which.max(date)],
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(year, quarter) |>
  mutate(treasury_10y_change_bp = (treasury_10y_end - lag(treasury_10y_end)) * 100) |>
  filter(year >= START_YEAR)
dgs10_q
```

### Stock prices (one row per REIT per quarter)

We keep the last trading day of each quarter. The quarterly total return is the change in
the adjusted close from the last quarter-end. The extra December data pulled in `01` is
what lets Q1 of the first year have a return.

```{r clean-prices}
prices_q = prices_raw |>
  filter(!is.na(adjusted)) |>
  distinct(symbol, date, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(lubridate::year(date)), quarter = as.integer(lubridate::quarter(date))) |>
  group_by(symbol, year, quarter) |>
  slice_max(date, n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(symbol, year, quarter) |>
  group_by(symbol) |>
  mutate(total_return_q_pct = (adjusted / lag(adjusted) - 1) * 100) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(year >= START_YEAR) |>
  transmute(ticker = symbol, year, quarter, quarter_end_trade_date = date,
            close_price = close, total_return_q_pct)

# the latest quarter is not over yet, so drop it (it would be a partial quarter)
current_q = lubridate::year(Sys.Date()) * 10 + lubridate::quarter(Sys.Date())
prices_q = prices_q |> filter(year * 10 + quarter < current_q)
dgs10_q  = dgs10_q  |> filter(year * 10 + quarter < current_q)
prices_q |> count(ticker)
```

## Save the cleaned data

```{r save}
readr::write_csv(nareit_clean,  file.path(proc_dir, "clean_nareit_reits.csv"))
readr::write_csv(sec_clean,     file.path(proc_dir, "clean_sec_quarterly.csv"))
readr::write_csv(llm_clean,     file.path(proc_dir, "clean_press_release_metrics.csv"))
readr::write_csv(focus_by_reit, file.path(proc_dir, "clean_property_focus.csv"))
readr::write_csv(dgs10_q,       file.path(proc_dir, "clean_treasury_quarterly.csv"))
readr::write_csv(prices_q,      file.path(proc_dir, "clean_prices_quarterly.csv"))
```
